prompt: A triangle has a base of $12$ and a height of $5$. What is its area?
hint: Recall the area formula for a triangle. It uses the base and the height, with one extra factor that is easy to forget.

hints.text: Recall the area formula for a triangle. It uses the base and the height, with one extra factor that is easy to forget.
The area is half of base times height, so work out $\tfrac{1}{2}(12)(5)$. Multiplying $12$ by $5$ first makes it easy.
Since $12 \times 5 = 60$ and half of $60$ is $30$, the area of the triangle is $30$.

learningObjective: Compute the area of a triangle.
explanation: The area of a triangle is half the base times the height, so write $\tfrac{1}{2}(12)(5)$.
Multiply the base by the height to get $60$, then take half of that to get $30$.
The area of the triangle is $30$. Leaving out the half would give the area of the surrounding rectangle instead.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why the one-half is there
steps: Any triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height.
Draw the rectangle around it and the halving becomes obvious rather than memorized.
This also explains why the height must be perpendicular to the base — it is the side of that rectangle.
